image_description: A Rock Beauty fish (Holocanthus tricolor) swimming near a coral reef. The fish displays the characteristic black anterior body and head, transitioning to a golden yellow posterior body and tail with a distinct black margin on the caudal fin. The background consists of textured red and green corals.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The color pattern matches the taxonomy perfectly: black front half, yellow back half, and a vertical black bar separating them, plus a black rim on the tail.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Continuous dorsal fin with spiny anterior and soft-rayed posterior portions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin runs continuously along the back. While individual spines vs rays are hard to distinguish due to image quality, the structural continuity is present.
The anal fin is visible on the ventral side, mirroring the shape of the posterior dorsal fin.
The caudal fin is clearly rounded, not forked or lunate.
